# Phase 01.1 Plan 09: Re-skin the Auth Route Group Summary

Signup, login and password reset now render in the Cena system, laid out mobile-first at the 44px
floor, with every glyph on the `Icon` wrapper — and the three things on this surface that are
security controls rather than style preferences are each unchanged and now say so in the file a
careless edit would open.

## What Was Built

**The three page shells (Task 1).** The page margin ramps 16 → 24 → 32px instead of sitting at 24px
on a phone. The card is top-anchored with auto block margins rather than cross-axis centred. Signup's
consent row takes the touch floor. Every submit control gets the 24px pre-submit step the form rhythm
specifies. The three cross-link sentences move from the Label role to Body in muted ink. Signup's
spinner routes through `Icon`.

**The three client components (Task 2).** The same form rhythm across `LoginForm`,
`RequestPasswordResetForm` and `SetNewPasswordForm`; all three spinners on `Icon` at the 1.75 stroke
with their existing size and animation classes. `GoogleOneTap`'s stack moves to the 16px element
rhythm with the disabled control and its gate reason nested at the 8px step, and its consent row
takes the touch floor.

**Nothing else moved.** All six files changed layout, spacing, type role and glyph routing only. No
string value, no ordering, no shell width class, no control height override, no client boundary.

## The Hit-Area Defect This Plan Found

Plan 01.1-08 corrected `checkbox.tsx`'s expander from a 40×32 near-miss to a true 44×44
(`after:-inset-3.5`), and recorded that the correction creates a new obligation at every call site:
the expander now claims **14px beyond the painted box on every side**, so a row only as tall as one
line of label text leaks its hit area into whatever sits below.

Both consent rows in the product are exactly that shape, and both were affected:

| Row | Painted box | Row height before | Expander reach below row | Gap to next control | Overlap |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `GoogleOneTap` consent row | 16px at `mt-1` | ~20px (one label line) | 34px from row top | 8px (`gap-2`) | **~6px into the Google control** |
| `signup` consent row | 16px at `mt-1` | ~40px (label wraps) | 34px from row top | 16px (`gap-4`) | none, but only by accident of wrapping |

The `GoogleOneTap` case is the live one and it is the worse of the two: the control whose top the
checkbox's hit area would claim is the Google sign-in button — the very control the consent gate
exists to hold back. A thumb reaching for it at a wide viewport, where the label fits on one line,
could toggle consent off instead. `min-h-11` on both rows makes each row as tall as the hit area it
contains, so the two tile with neither overlap nor dead space. This is the same correction plan
01.1-08 applied to the venue form's language rows for the same reason.

The signup row is safe today only because its label wraps to two lines at the widths this card is
rendered at — a layout accident, not a property. It carries the floor now too.

## The Three Security Controls, and What Was Done About Each

The plan's threat register rates all three `high` with a `mitigate` disposition. The mitigation for
each is non-change, so what follows is evidence of non-change rather than of correctness.

| Threat | Control | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| T-01.1-05 | The shared signup/login error string | `git diff lib/copy.ts` empty; `grep -c 'COPY.errors.auth' login-form.tsx` = 1. Not split, not softened, not varied. |
| T-01.1-09 | Consent-gate ordering | Checkbox still precedes the control; the effect reaching Google is still gated on it. `tests/auth/google-affordance.test.tsx` and `tests/lib/google-affordance-coverage.test.ts` both green, run against these files specifically. |
| T-01.1-03 | The one allowlisted external origin | Occurrence count in `GoogleOneTap.tsx` identical before and after (1 → 1). `src`, loading strategy and both handlers untouched. `tests/theme/no-third-party-assets.test.ts` green — the allowlist still has exactly one entry. |
| T-01.1-35 | Auth logic changed under cover of a visual pass | The non-comment diff of `GoogleOneTap.tsx` is eight class strings and one fragment-to-`div` change. No auth logic, no session handling, no recovery-grant behaviour. The whole `tests/auth` directory green after each task. |

Each of the three now carries an in-file note at the place it lives, saying what it is and why a
later edit must not move it. Following the phase's own convention — and the trap that has cost three
plans — the note about the single external origin **describes** that origin rather than quoting it,
so the grep that proves the allowlist has not grown cannot match the comment explaining it.

## Deviations from Plan

### Auto-fixed during execution

**1. [Rule 2 - Missing critical functionality] `min-h-11` on both consent rows.**
- **Found during:** Task 1 (signup) and Task 2 (GoogleOneTap), while checking the 44px floor was not
  overridden down.
- **Issue:** the full analysis is in the table above. In short, plan 01.1-08's corrected checkbox
  expander reaches 14px past the painted box on every side, and neither consent row was tall enough
  to contain it. On `GoogleOneTap` at a wide viewport the overspill lands on the Google sign-in
  control — a mis-tap that toggles consent off while the owner believes they pressed sign-in.
- **Fix:** `min-h-11` on each row. The painted checkbox is unchanged at 16px.
- **Commits:** `6cb594b` (signup), `a933f10` (GoogleOneTap).

**2. [Rule 2 - Missing critical functionality] The auth shells are top-anchored, not centred.**
- **Found during:** Task 1, working through the E11 overflow backstop at 320px.
- **Issue:** all three shells used cross-axis centring inside a `min-h-full` flex parent. A centred
  flex child that outgrows its container overflows in **both** directions, so the top of the card —
  the title and the first field — becomes unreachable by scrolling. Raising every control to the
  44px floor is what makes this real: the signup form is comfortably over 500px tall before the
  Google affordance, against a 320×568 viewport.
- **Fix:** `items-start` on the parent plus `my-auto` on the card wrapper. Auto block margins centre
  the card when there is free space and resolve to zero when there is not, so the visual result at
  desktop is unchanged and the phone case scrolls normally.
- **Commit:** `6cb594b`.

**3. [Rule 1 - Bug, self-inflicted] A JSX comment placed in expression position.**
- **Found during:** Task 1, on the first test run after editing `reset-password/page.tsx`.
- **Issue:** a `{/* … */}` comment was written immediately inside a ternary's parenthesised branch,
  which is not JSX children position. The parser reported it against the `<p>` that followed.
- **Fix:** moved the comment above the ternary, where it is a JSX child. Caught before any commit.

### Scope boundaries recorded rather than acted on

**4. Inline text links are not raised to the 44px floor, and the reason is not laziness.**
The plan's truth list says no interactive control on these surfaces sits below a 44px hit area, and
a `<Link>` is interactive. The UI-SPEC's floor enumeration, though, names painted controls — button,
chip, pill, checkbox, switch, tab, select trigger, menu row — and the mechanism for a small control
is a pseudo-element expander around it. The concrete case is the recovery link beside the password
label in `login-form.tsx`: reaching 44px from a ~20px text line needs 12px per side, which is more
than the 8px between that row and the password input, so the link's hit area would claim the top of
the field and a thumb reaching for the password would navigate away. That is precisely the mis-tap
the floor exists to prevent. The link keeps its typographic size, and the reasoning is written into
the file rather than left to be rediscovered. **This is the one item on this plan worth a human eye
at the browser pass.**

**5. The `Field` family was deliberately not adopted.**
`components/ui/field.tsx`'s header asks whichever of plans 01.1-09..12 first composes a `<Field>` to
record the answer. This plan composes none. Two reasons: `components/ui/field.tsx` is outside this
plan's `files_modified` and three sibling agents are editing adjacent surfaces concurrently, so
recording an answer there would be an out-of-scope write; and the reconciliation already names
`components/field-error.tsx` as the owner of error presentation for every `useActionState` + Zod form
in the repo, which is all six of these. Adopting `Field` here would buy layout the existing
`flex flex-col gap-2` already provides, at the cost of migrating a message shape that is correct. The
question stays open for plans 01.1-10..12.

**6. The Card size and the shell width classes were not touched**, as the plan directs. `max-w-md`
resolves correctly only because `app/globals.css` carries matching width shields; the reason is now
restated in `signup/page.tsx` and `login/page.tsx` so the next reader meets it at the call site.

## Type-Role Changes, Stated Plainly

Four `<p>` elements moved from the Label role (14px/600) to Body in muted ink (16px/400). Each is a
sentence — two cross-links, one recovery cross-link, one gate reason — and a sentence set at
semibold 14px reads as a label. This follows the treatment `field.tsx`'s `FieldDescription` already
gives body copy with a link, including the rule that a link in body copy is marked by its underline
and never by the accent. No string changed; only the role assigned to it.

`CardTitle className="text-display"` was left exactly as it was on all three pages. `CardTitle`
already carries `font-heading`, so these titles were already Display in the serif family.

is 728/728 now. No test was added, modified, skipped or weakened. Two full runs during this plan each
showed a single transient failure that passed on immediate re-run with no source change — consistent
with the two known-flaky live-Postgres files, and green on the final three consecutive runs.

**One environment note for the verifier:** `tests/theme/build-assets.test.ts` reads the compiled
`.next` output, so it fails in a fresh worktree until `pnpm build` has been run once. That is a
tooling ordering fact, not a defect, and it accounted for the 5 failures on the very first baseline
attempt.

## Icon Migration Coverage

This route group has three surface call sites, all now on the wrapper: `signup/page.tsx`,
`login-form.tsx` and `password-reset-forms.tsx`, one spinner glyph each. `login/page.tsx`,
`reset-password/page.tsx` and `GoogleOneTap.tsx` render no glyph and correctly import none. The glyph
identifier is still imported from `lucide-react` and passed to the wrapper as a prop, which is the
shape plan 01.1-07 specified. This plan claims 3 of the 14 surface call sites; the remaining 11
belong to plans 01.1-10, 01.1-11 and 01.1-12.

## Known Stubs

None. No placeholder, TODO, empty-value default or unwired data path was introduced. A grep of the
route group for stub markers returns nothing.

## Threat Flags

None. This plan introduced no network endpoint, no auth path, no file access pattern and no schema
change. The one pre-existing trust boundary it touches — the browser to the single allowlisted
external origin — is byte-identical, gated, and now documented in place.
